finding.summary: Unbounded-range expansion is not size-capped: explicit endpoints bypass the "clamp to data extent" guarantee, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion (DoS) from a single formula, amplified to all collaborators via buildDependantsMap
finding.evidence: `resolveRange` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts, new function) only substitutes the *omitted* half of an endpoint from `bounds` — explicitly written parts are passed through unclamped: `toRange({r: a.r ?? 1, c: a.c ?? 1}, {r: b.r ?? max.r, c: b.c ?? max.c})`. The new grammar (packages/sheets/antlr/Formula.g4) makes `ROW: '$'? [1-9][0-9]*` and `COL` (up to 3 letters, i.e. up to ZZZ = 18278) legal *range endpoints on their own*, so `=SUM(1:99999999)` lexes as one REFRANGE and resolves to rows 1..99,999,999 × cols 1..maxC, and `=SUM(A:ZZZ)` resolves to 18,278 columns × maxR rows. Every downstream consumer then materialises that range cell-by-cell: `toSrefs(extractReferences(...))` in MemStore.buildDependantsMap (packages/sheets/src/store/memory.ts, changed line) and three times in YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts ~565-605), plus `Arguments.iterate`'s `for (const ref of toSrefs([node.v]))` (packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts). Attack: a user types one formula (or, in the collaborative YorkieStore document, any participant does) — buildDependantsMap is rebuilt on every edit and will allocate one Map/Set entry per cell of the expanded range, hanging or OOM-ing every client sharing the document. Even the fully-omitted form is cheap to weaponise: place one value at a far row (e.g. row 1,000,000) so `getUsedBounds()`/`CellIndex.bounds()` reports maxR=1,000,000, then `=SUM(A:A)` expands to a million refs per formula. I could not open the working tree (Glob/Grep returned no files in /tmp/eval-item-hRoO8Z/repo), so I could not confirm the absence of a size cap inside `toSrefs`/`fetchGridByReferences`; hence medium confidence. No cap appears anywhere in the diff, and the new docs (docs/design/sheets/formula.md) assert ranges are "clamped to the sheet's data extent", which is only true for omitted endpoints.
